title: MariaDB TLS key exchange
text: MariaDB 12.3 negotiates ECDH on P-521 (secp521r1); Percona Server uses P-256. Much of the extra client CPU per TLS connect on MariaDB is that server-side choice, not the driver.

title: TLS without a CA loads the system trust store
text: With no CA configured, libmysqlclient, MariaDB Connector/C and the drivers built on them (Connector/C++, mysqlclient, MariaDB Connector/Python, Ruby mysql2) and trilogy load and parse the full system CA bundle (120 certificates) on every connection although they verify nothing.

title: Different default authentication
text: Each server uses its own default authentication: Percona Server caching_sha2_password (SHA-256 plus an extra round trip on the fast path), MariaDB mysql_native_password. Part of the Percona-vs-MariaDB difference in plain connect cost comes from this, not the driver.

title: Connector/C sleeps after connect()
text: MariaDB Connector/C calls usleep(1) after every connect() (about 50 µs on Linux). This adds wall time per connection, not CPU.

title: Percona converts JSON on every read
text: Percona Server (like MySQL) stores JSON in a binary format and converts it to text on every read: about 13× the server CPU of the same bytes as LONGBLOB, and ~10% larger output. The slower send makes most clients spend more CPU per KB than reading the same documents from MariaDB, which stores JSON as text.

title: Returns JSON as bytes on Percona
text: MariaDB Connector/Python returns Percona's JSON column as raw bytes (no UTF-8 decoding) but MariaDB's JSON column as a decoded string. Not comparable with other drivers or across servers.

title: Two TLS reads per row
text: libmysqlclient issues two SSL_read calls per row (2M for 1M rows; MariaDB Connector/C about 700), so TLS doubles its per-row cost.

title: MariaDB-only bulk protocol
text: On MariaDB this uses the bulk-execute protocol (COM_STMT_BULK_EXECUTE). Percona Server does not have it, so the driver falls back to one execute per row there, or the test is n/a.

title: Connector/J batch defaults
text: With default settings Connector/J's executeBatch() sends one INSERT per row; rewriteBatchedStatements=true (tuned) rewrites the batch into multi-row INSERTs.

title: Fails, not unsupported
text: go-sql-driver advertises ed25519 support but fails against MariaDB 12.3 with "malformed packet" (go-mysql works with the same account). A driver bug, not a missing feature.

title: Three round trips per parameterized query
text: Without client-side interpolation (go-sql-driver: interpolateParams=true, tuned) each parameterized call prepares, executes and closes a server-side statement.

title: Three round trips per parameterized query
text: go-mysql's Conn.Execute(sql, args...) prepares, executes and closes a server-side statement on every call.

title: PyMySQL enables TLS by default
text: Without TLS options PyMySQL negotiates TLS whenever the server offers it, creating a TLS context and loading the system CA bundle on every connection (about 3.7 ms of CPU). The non-TLS results here pass ssl_disabled=True. An earlier version of this report showed PyMySQL's TLS-by-default cost as its plain connect cost; that was a mistake in the benchmark, corrected on 2026-11-21.

title: Runs out of memory
text: With as: :array and cache_rows: false, mysql2 kept growing past the 8 GB client cap on 100 KB documents and was killed (on both servers; before the cap existed it pushed the host into the kernel OOM killer twice). Results that are not freed explicitly hold their C buffers, which Ruby's garbage collector does not account for.

title: Higher run-to-run spread
text: The 5 processes for this result differ by more than 5% (coefficient of variation). Small differences against it are not meaningful.

title: Warm-up did not fully settle
text: In at least one of the 5 processes the per-iteration cost never came within 5% for 3 iterations in a row before the 40-iteration cap, usually because of garbage collection. The figure is the median of steady-state iterations, but treat small differences as approximate.
